source: GauravSh-7/nse-trading-holidays-2018-2026 (MIT; the founder-designated in-app source, 13 Oct 2026) — community-compiled, README: 'independently compiled and cross-verified against official NSE India holiday calendars and exchange circulars' for 2018-2026; segment NSE F&O; weekday rows extracted (their weekend rows are handled by lib/marketHours.ts, not this file). Offline cross-check (tooling only, NOT in the app): pandas_market_calendars (MIT) holidays/nse.py @ 9af1144af406eac48bb113692d81fe33b3f20589, whose stated upstream is NSE's published holiday circulars. The two sources agree on all 15 dates carried here. One disputed date — 2026-01-15 (Makar Sankranti), a closed day per pandas_market_calendars but a trading day per the designated source — is EXCLUDED pending the NSE-circular check: the exchange page is unreachable from the build environment (Akamai 403, docs/evidence/round55/), and the fail-closed direction is to omit a disputed closed-day (a missing holiday can only cause extra quote refreshes and a stricter probe; a false holiday would silence the 15-minute freshness rule on a live session). The December ritual resolves this date against NSE's official list before January. Holiday and session dates are facts; the MIT licenses cover the upstream code and this attribution carries the provenance (C1/FD-15).
scope: 2026 calendar year, weekday closures only (weekends are handled separately by lib/marketHours.ts). Muhurat special sessions (Diwali evening) are NOT modelled. The annual December ritual adds the next year and re-diffs the full list against NSE's official list (including the disputed 2026-01-15) before January (docs/DATA_SOURCES.md row 16). A year outside this scope degrades to weekend-only behavior: extra quote refreshes on unknown holidays, never a wrong label.
